title: How to (Accidentally) Meet the British Pakistani Kids of London. Tip #1
body: Ask what they're studying and there are four acceptable answers. Medicine, dentistry, pharmacy, or law, and if it's anything else there was a conversation about it in 2021 that everybody remembers. It's a sealed deal if a cousin doing medicine gets mentioned within eleven minutes of meeting the parents.
caption:
Tip #1 😭 medicine, dentistry, pharmacy or law. Pick one.

title: How to (Accidentally) Meet the British Pakistani Kids of London. Tip #2
body: Watch the accent switch, because it happens mid-sentence and they don't notice. Full London with their mates, softened for a teacher, and something else entirely on the phone to a grandmother in Lahore. Three registers, no effort. It's a sealed deal if they say "innit" and "jazakallah" in the same breath.

Tip #2 😭 medicine, dentistry, pharmacy or law. Pick one.

title: How to (Accidentally) Meet the British Pakistani Kids of London. Tip #3
body: Ask about the 11+ and watch a childhood come back. Three years of tutoring on Saturdays in someone's front room in Ilford, a result the whole extended family knows, and a school that decided the next decade. It's a sealed deal if they still remember which questions they got wrong sixteen years later.

title: How to (Accidentally) Meet the British Pakistani Kids of London. Tip #4
body: Ask where they eat and the answer separates generations. The parents say Royal Nawaab and mean it. The kids say Dishoom in public and Tayyabs in private. Everyone agrees on Lahore Kebab House and nobody agrees on which branch. It's a sealed deal if a family has been going to the same place on Green Street since 1998.

title: How to (Accidentally) Meet the British Pakistani Kids of London. Tip #5
body: Watch how they talk about going back, because that word carries a lot. Their passport is British. They've been eight times. They call it going home because their parents do, and they cannot navigate the city they say it about. It's a sealed deal if the only address they could find there is a grandmother's street.

title: How to (Accidentally) Meet the British Pakistani Kids of London. Tip #6
body: Ask about the car at eighteen and the family reveals itself. A Corolla the father chose deliberately as a lesson. A Golf if the parents caved. A Mercedes if nobody was teaching anything. All three exist in the same postcode. It's a sealed deal if the insurance cost more than the car and everybody has a story about it.

title: How to (Accidentally) Meet the British Pakistani Kids of London. Tip #7
body: Watch Ramadan, because it is the one month the whole community synchronises. Taraweeh at the same mosque as their father did, iftar at four different houses in one week, and Eid clothes ordered from back home in February. It's a sealed deal if the same eight families have broken fast together every year since the kids were small.

title: How to (Accidentally) Meet the British Pakistani Kids of London. Tip #8
body: Ask about the rishta conversation and see how fast it turns awkward. The parents have a list. There is an aunty with a folder. Half of them are on Muzz and have told nobody. All three systems are running at once and everybody is pretending only one exists. It's a sealed deal if a proposal has been quietly ended by a group chat screenshot.
